Nifty 50 Reclaims 25,000, Sensex Surges Over 1,700 Points on 7th Day of Gains
sum: At the close, the Sensex settled at 81,028.03, up 1,718.02 points or 2.17 per cent, while the Nifty 50 ended at 25,030.35, higher by 493.75 points or 2.01 per cent.

Market Update at 04:00 PM: Indian benchmark indices extended their winning streak to a seventh consecutive session on Friday, November 6, 2026, supported by sustained foreign institutional investor (FII) buying, strong quarterly earnings and renewed interest in heavyweight Banking stocks. The rally came despite a sharp selloff in global technology stocks.

FIIs remained a major driver of the recovery. On Thursday, November 5, they bought shares worth Rs 14,974.68 crore, their largest single-day net purchase in nearly six years. Domestic institutional investors were net sellers of equities worth Rs 10,444.54 crore.

Lower crude oil prices also supported sentiment. Brent crude slipped below USD 100 per barrel earlier this week on expectations of easing tensions in the Middle East following the U.S. midterm elections. Cheaper crude reduces India’s import bill, eases inflationary pressure and improves the outlook for industries dependent on petroleum-based raw materials.

Indian equities showed relative strength despite a sharp overnight decline on Wall Street and weakness across Asia. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.52 per cent and the S&P 500 fell around 4.36 per cent on Thursday, amid concerns over artificial intelligence investments and technology-sector valuations. Asian markets followed on Friday, with South Korea’s KOSPI falling around 8 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei dropping about 5 per cent in morning trade. Indian indices still attracted buying, backed by domestic earnings and foreign inflows.

Corporate earnings added to the momentum. Mahindra & Mahindra reported a 25 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 4,588 crore for Q2 FY27, while consolidated revenue rose about 25 per cent to Rs 57,553 crore, driven by strong growth in its automobile business. The shares gained 5.11 per cent, making the company one of the leading gainers among Nifty 50 constituents.
Broader markets did not join the rally, as selling pressure continued in midcap and smallcap stocks.

sum: Iran's chief negotiator with the United States, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, said the outcome of the US midterm elections showed that Americans had rejected war, as he commented on the apparent prospect of President Donald Trump's Republican Party losing its

Financial markets reacted quickly to the Democratic sweep of the U.S. midterm elections. As results came in overnight, the dollar weakened against every major currency, technology stocks fell sharply and gold climbed above USD4,000 an ounce. Analysts said the moves reflected two expectations: a Democratic Congress will rein in government spending and it will scrutinize the artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency industries more closely.

The dollar index, which measures the U.S. currency against a basket of six others, fell about 0.3% to 101.4 by Wednesday morning in Asia, Reuters reported. The euro rose 0.5% to USD1.1249, sterling gained 0.4% to USD1.3460 and the yen strengthened 0.7% to 157.63 per dollar. The sharpest move was against the Swiss franc, where the dollar dropped 0.9%. By 07:00 Central European Time, Euronews put the euro at USD1.1232, still up 0.4% on the day.

Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said a Democratic sweep “would limit government spending,” which could push the dollar lower. Moh Siong Sim of Singapore’s OCBC said the selling reflected concern that Democrats would bring greater regulatory scrutiny of AI, hitting the Nasdaq and U.S. growth prospects, although he noted that “it is still difficult to pass legislation at the federal level” while Trump holds a veto.

Not everyone expects the move to last. Analysts at the Dutch bank ING wrote that “the greenback continues to respond predominantly to the Fed story,” meaning that interest-rate decisions by the Federal Reserve will matter more for the currency than the balance of power in Congress.

Stock markets fell harder than currencies. U.S. futures for the S&P 500 dropped about 1.1% by early Wednesday, Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.9% and Dow futures fell 0.7%, according to The National. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei lost 3.5% and South Korea’s KOSPI fell 3.6%, erasing gains of more than 3% earlier in the session. Futures on Europe’s Euro Stoxx 50 and Germany’s DAX pointed to a drop of about 0.5% at the open.

WA minister shares vile voice message as concerns grow over MPs’ safety
sum: Creative Industries Minister Simone McGurk has shared a vulgar message left on her office answering machine in a demonstration of the regular vitriol West Australian MPs and their electorate office staff face.

Speaking at a Business News breakfast on Tuesday morning, McGurk vented her frustration at the current state of political debate in Australia, revealing the frequent aggression MPs and political staff received.
The message shared by McGurk was from an American man seemingly upset at the member for Fremantle’s past commentary about US politics.
He opens with the greeting, “Hello, you horrible f----ing witch”, before telling her to “shut up about American politics”, and describes Australia as a “prison colony” and “inbred”.
McGurk said it was important people understood the sort of vitriol and aggression that many elected representatives and their staff received.
“I think women get it in particular, but it really does extend to a lot of elected representatives,” she said.
“It’s really vulgar. It’s aggressive. It’s unacceptable by any measure. Sadly, that then extends to real life, where in my electorate office we will often get calls.”

sum: For most lay investors, this is uncharted territory. But for the market mavens at India’s mutual fund companies, this is hunting season.

Even as pessimism grips the broader market, these fund manag ers are seeing fertile ground for finding new investable opportunities as well as compelling entry points for high-conviction names. In this 13th edition of our special Most Wanted Stocks feature, we have zeroed in on a few stocks that have been consistently favoured by fund managers. The six stocks we have shortlisted have seen a gradual rise in mutual fund holdings for four consecutive quarters since September 2025. For a detailed look at how we zeroed in on these names, refer to the methodology on page 7.

Keep in mind that mimicking fund managers’ big moves comes with caveats. They often build positions gradually at lower valua tions and exit swiftly when market conditions or fundamentals change. Investors should do their own due diligence and invest only surplus money they won’t need for the next few years.

KFintech mainly serves the operational needs of as set managers with clients spanning mutual funds, alternative investment funds (AIFs), pension funds, and wealth managers. In its MF business, revenue growth has been slower amid a shift towards lower-yield liquid funds and a provision for an upcoming contract renewal. The management is keen on expanding the addressable market and diversifying revenue mix by reduc ing the contribution of domestic MF business to around 50% over the next three years.

The international business segment has seen several large deal wins as the company shifted its strategy from focusing on small boutique managers to large clients. With the integration of Singapore-based Ascent Funds Services (acquired recently), the management expects better yields and profitability led by new client wins and improving asset under management (AUM) growth in the Southeast Asian business.

Polish consumers keep spending, but momentum softens
sum: Retail sales were slightly weaker, but not disappointing. This can be explained by the absence of the fuel discount programme (CPN) in September and slowing real wage growth. On the other hand, sales of durable goods continue to grow at a solid pace

Retail sales rose by 3.3% year-on-year in September (ING: 4.2%; consensus: 3.6%) following a 3.8% YoY increase in August. Seasonally adjusted data indicates that sales rose by 1.7% month-on-month. Today’s figures complete the picture for the third quarter and suggest that, despite high fuel prices at petrol stations, private consumption remains relatively resilient. Contributing factors include temporary government interventions in the fuel market (periodic reductions in excise duty and VAT rates) and accumulated savings.

A closer look at retail sales data for recent months suggests, however, that the picture for Polish consumers remains mixed. On the one hand, sales of durable goods continue to record solid double-digit growth. The largest increases were seen in sales of motor vehicles and parts (13.1% YoY), furniture, consumer electronics and household appliances (10.7% YoY), and pharmaceuticals (8.5% YoY). Poland has one of the lowest shares of new cars in the EU, so the vehicle fleet is still being renewed, partly thanks to inexpensive Chinese brands.

At the other end of the spectrum are sales trends for essential goods, such as food and fuel (up 1.4% YoY, the category with the largest share of retail sales), and textiles (down 3.0% YoY). It is worth noting that the fuel discount programme (CPN) was not in effect in September (it was introduced at the end of the summer holidays in August and resumed in early October), which may explain weak fuel sales.

Another possible explanation is the differing consumption patterns of higher-income individuals with accumulated savings and less affluent consumers. In this context, the slowing pace of real wage growth is important. It is worth recalling that the real wage bill grew by 1.3% YoY in September, the slowest rate in more than three years.
Consumer confidence weighs on 2026 consumption but so far only slightly
Today’s data confirms that private consumption remained an important driver of economic growth in 3Q26.

Deutsche Bank lists Top European Stock picks for the next twelve months
sum: Investing.com -- Deutsche Bank on Thursday named its top European stock picks for the next 12 months, adding six new names and dropping six from its third-quarter list.
The broker added ING, SPIE, ICG, UCB, Groupe ADP and RWE, replacing Barclays, Bunzl, Euronext, Novartis, International Airlines Group and E.ON. Deutsche Bank did not give reasons for the changes.
It also had no top pick in the consumer staples categories covering household and personal care and food, where Henkel was its previous choice. All stocks on the new list carry a "buy" rating.

Groupe ADP is among the new picks, with a €130 price target versus a Sept. 29 close of €110. Deutsche Bank said a proposed regulatory agreement with the French government should provide greater visibility on the airport operator's business through 2034. It expects regulatory approval around November, which could act as a near-term catalyst.

Sixteen stocks remained on the list, including Safran, Volkswagen, Heidelberg Materials, Siemens Energy, SYENSQO, Coca-Cola Hellenic, Novonesis, British American Tobacco, Adidas, Entain, Scout24, Lonza, Thyssenkrupp, Merlin Properties, Technoprobe, SAP and Orange.

Among the continuing picks, Deutsche Bank sees potential for Siemens Energy to increase its share buyback programme from €6 billion to as much as €12 billion in November. It has a €210 price target, compared with a €146 close.

Safran's spare-parts sales rose 28% and services revenue increased 40% in the first half of 2026, both well ahead of expectations, Deutsche Bank said. The stock closed at €335, against the bank's €398 target.

sum: Will Arnett reveals why he's 'very happy' with his life these days
During the latest episode of his SmartLess podcast, the 56-year-old actor and comedian revealed that he's "very happy” with his life these days.
“It’s going really well,” Will told his co-hosts Jason Bateman and Sean Hayes.
As his friends demanded he “talk about secrets,” the LEGO Masters star responded, "Both of you know exactly what’s happening, and I’m not going to walk into your trap.”
“I’m very happy, very, very happy,” Will added. “Things are going great.”
Last month, People magazine reported that the comedian is in a relationship with Emma Marciano. For those unaware, Emma is the co-founder of the fashion label, Mimchik, based in Los Angeles.
During the podcast, Jason asked Will, “In a perfect world, in five years, what does this relationship look like?"
